analysis: Examined three changes. (1) ProviderLoop+StartupPreload.swift head 304-310: finishStartupPreload now calls enqueueSelectedModelRecovery for skippedInsufficientMemory, failedInsufficientMemory and notAttempted candidates. It is guarded by !Task.isCancelled, !isShuttingDown and !startupPreloadStopRequested. Self-test-failed and retired ids are not passed, and the plan is filtered through advertisedModels (lines 148-151). The recovery implementation, ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery, is not supplied. Integration must verify four points: recovery uses a no-eviction load; it honors the add-on hold and model-load fence (TB-012/T-059/A-018), noting persistLoadedModelSet line 106 and the gate log at line 197 suggest holds defer loads; it refuses ids in failedSelfTestHashes/retiringModels (isRefusedByRetirement line 483); and it stops on servingDrain.refusing. Without that source, no regression is proven. (2) ProviderLoop+StartupShutdown.swift head 61, 78-97: the unbounded unload loop (base 61-69) is replaced with a per-slot 15s bounded wait. Slots whose retirement does not finish are abandoned, and shutdown returns true with them still resident. performPreRegistrationShutdown already set isShuttingDown, cancelled inflight work and shut down the coordinator client before this point, so no new routing or plaintext exposure is visible. Abandoned slots' memory (A-001 residue, T-028) is released on process exit. The open question is whether every caller of shutdownBeforeRegistration, including the schedule-window close, actually exits the process. If one does not, a resident abandoned slot could coexist with a later load, which is an availability concern. The unloadModel Task continues after the timeout; ShutdownUnloadFlag is lock-guarded. (3) ProviderLoop+Testing.swift head 514-525 adds test seams setSelectedModelRecoveryLoadOverrideForTesting and awaitSelectedModelRecoveryAttemptForTesting. They are not DEBUG-gated, matching the existing seam pattern, and are only reachable via internal access. No new external surface. No concrete regression was identified.
